summary: Five OpenSpec changes written for phase-9, reviewed together across 13 adversarial rounds (30 findings, 30/30 accepted, final PASS). Two scope changes came out of the review rather than the plan: externalUrl was DROPPED after grepping the shipped packages showed no text/uri-list mimeType anywhere, and the schema's mimeType literals were corrected to text/html;profile=mcp-app — the MCP Apps spelling both @mcp-ui/client and @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps actually emit.

changes.summary: direct:mcp-ui enum entry, mcp-ui-resource.schema.json, domain adapter, routing
normalize-mcp-ui.mjs with a schema-path override and four named violations plus a residual
example corpus — 2 positive, 5 negative, each well-formed except its one defect
AppRenderer surface, resource store, Vite mock, sandbox proxy, trust-boundary tests

scope_changes_from_analyze.why: Analyze Q3 presumed it was a mimeType variant a schema could support cheaply. Upstream models it as a distinct content shape ({type:'externalUrl', iframeUrl}), and grepping @mcp-ui/client@7.1.1 and @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.5 found NO text/uri-list mimeType in either. Supporting it would have meant inventing a wire format — the exact failure mode phases 7 and 8 spent themselves correcting.
scope_changes_from_analyze.impact: One delivery mode in scope: inline HTML, in two admitted mimeType spellings.

scope_changes_from_analyze.why: text/html;profile=mcp-app is what both shipped packages emit — verified by grep. My first schema draft used bare text/html and text/uri-list; the latter exists in neither package.
scope_changes_from_analyze.impact: Branch A is the MCP Apps spelling (what p9-04's live gate drives); branch B is bare text/html for legacy producers.

scope_changes_from_analyze.what: remoteDom rejection is structural, not mimeType-based
scope_changes_from_analyze.why: There is no remoteDom mimeType to exclude — upstream carries it as {type:'remoteDom', script, framework}.
scope_changes_from_analyze.impact: Rejected via additionalProperties plus a named unsupported_content_shape violation.

open_questions_resolved_here: Q1 (sandbox origin) — serve the proxy same-origin AND override permissions to drop allow-same-origin, keeping the no-second-process property. p9-04 gate 5.2 asserts the rendered attribute; if the handshake breaks without it, fall back to a second origin and DO NOT restore the permissive default.

Q2 (AppRenderer vs AppFrame) — AppRenderer with pre-fetched html, which keeps the mock at three JSON-RPC methods. p9-04 task 3.2 verifies that empirically against the running app rather than trusting the types.
Q3 (externalUrl in v1) — no; see scope_changes_from_analyze.
Q4 (which change owns the trust-boundary gates) — p9-04 owns all five, and its task 7.1 states explicitly that the standing no-hardcoded-secrets gate does NOT scan assets/.
carry_forward_for_plan: p9-04 is the largest change and carries every trust-boundary gate plus the browser-DOM gate. Its dependency chain (2.8a → 4.2 → 6.5 → 2.8b → {5.4, 6.5b}) is acyclic but NOT in section order; the plan must not reorder it.
p9-05 depends on BOTH p9-03 and p9-04. Declaring only p9-04 would leave the graph satisfiable without the corpus — the exact hole review caught in phase-8's p8-05.
p9-01 and p9-02 both need a validator before p9-02's normalizer exists; p9-01 §4 names a scratchpad harness importing normalize-a2ui.mjs's validator (the one with real oneOf after phase-8).
Do NOT add the new skill to .claude-plugin/plugin.json. It has no skills key; CLAUDE.md:54 is the stale half of a contradiction flagged since phase-7, and p8-05 declined the same edit.

adversarial_review.packet_assembly: manual — build-review-packet.sh supports only the native-kbd spec layout
adversarial_review.cap_rationale: Rounds 1-8 were still producing 3-5 CRITICALs each, and they were substantive: an unbuildable fixture, a gate that would fail on a blank page, schema literals no shipped package emits. Rounds 9-12 shifted to catching defects my own fixes had introduced. Round 13 returned PASS with one WARNING — the convergence signal.
adversarial_review.highest_value_finding: Round 6 asked for the actual remoteDom mimeType literal. Grepping the installed packages to answer it revealed the MCP Apps spelling (text/html;profile=mcp-app) and the total absence of text/uri-list — which invalidated BOTH schema branches I had written and removed externalUrl from scope entirely.

recurring_pattern: COVERAGE CLAIMED OVER THE WRONG PATH, third phase running. Round 2 caught p9-01 and p9-05 both asserting the no-hardcoded-secrets gate covered SKILL.md and skills/, which it does not scan — written into tasks that cite phase-8's identical failure. Knowing the lesson did not prevent repeating it; the check did. Every constraint claim now names uncovered files and carries a runnable grep.
tooling_gaps: build-review-packet.sh handles only the native-kbd spec layout; OpenSpec change sets must be assembled by hand. Flagged in phase-8, still open.
The packet includes neither decision-log.md nor a phase evidence/ directory, so operator decisions and vendored upstream artifacts are invisible to the judge.
runtime_note: G-7 runtime write-drop still in force; filesystem is authoritative.
